questions.question: As per the Census data, What was the density of population in India in 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**382 persons/sq km.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **density of population** in India is calculated by **dividing the total population** of India by the **total area of the country.**
 
• As per the **2011 Census**, the total population of India was **1.21 billion** and the total area was **3.17 million sq km.**
 
• Therefore, the density of population in India in **2011** was **382 persons/sq km.**
 
• This density is **relatively high**, considering the fact that India is the **second-most populous **country in the world after China.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **definition of a census** is the process of **gathering and recording data** regarding the population. 
 
• The first comprehensive census was done in **1881,** but it had been conducted every ten years since** Viceroy Lord Mayo** took office in **1872.**
 
• Since **1949, **it has been managed by the **Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India,** through the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.

questions.question: Pectin, which is responsible for the firmness and softness of fruits, is mainly composed of which acid unit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Galacturonic acid.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pectin **is a **complex carbohydrate** that is found in the** cell walls of plants **and is responsible for the **firmness and softness of fruits.**
 
• The main acid unit that makes up pectin is** galacturonic acid,** which is a** sugar acid **that is derived from **glucose.**
 
• Pectin is made up of **complex polysaccharides,** which are widely distributed in the **green parts of terrestrial plants** and found in the primary cell walls of plants.
 
• The main element of the **middle lamella,** where pectin binds cells, is pectin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aspartic acid** is an **amino acid** that is not found in pectin**, **but is found in **proteins.**

 
 
• **Lentils, soybeans, garbanzo beans**, and other** legumes **are plant sources of aspartic acid. 
 
 
 
• **Lactic acid** is a** simple organic acid** that is produced by bacteria during** fermentation** and is not found in pectin.
 
 
• Our body creates lactic acid when our cells** digest carbohydrates** for energy.
 
 
 
• **Glutamic acid** is an** amino acid t**hat is not found in pectin, but is found in **proteins.**
 
 
• It transforms into** glutamate **inside the body.
 
• This substance aids in the transmission and reception of information between** brain nerve cells.**​

questions.question: Sporophyte stage is dominant in which plant group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vascular plants.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **sporophyte stage** is the dominant phase in** vascular plants,** which includes all plants **except bryophytes **(mosses, liverworts, and hornworts).
 
• In **bryophytes,** the **gametophyte stage** is the dominant phase, while the **sporophyte** is dependent on the gametophyte for **survival. **
 
• **Algae **do not have a well-defined **alternation of generations,** and their life cycles can vary greatly depending on the type of algae.
 
• **Pteridophytes**, which include** ferns and horsetails, **have a **dominant sporophyte stage** that is independent of the gametophyte.
 
• The** dominance of the sporophyte stage** is characterized by the fact that it is the stage that produces the** spores,** which give rise to the next generation of plants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bryophytes **are small,** non-vascular plants** that grow in damp habitats.

 
 
• They** do not** have true roots, stems, or leaves and rely on diffusion to transport water and nutrients.
 
 
 
• **Algae **are a diverse group of **aquatic organisms** that can range from **single-celled organisms** to large seaweeds.
 
 
• They are not considered to be** true plants **because they **lack specialized tissues and organs.**
 
 
 
• **Pteridophytes** are** vascular plants **that reproduce by **spores **instead of seeds.
 
 
• They have** true roots, stems, and leaves,** and can range from small herbaceous plants to large tree ferns.
 
 
 
• The **alternation of generations** is a life cycle that includes both a **haploid (n) gametophyte and a diploid (2n)** sporophyte stage.
 
 
• In plants, the gametophyte produces **gametes (eggs and sperm),** which fuse to form a **diploid zygote** that develops into the sporophyte.
 
• The sporophyte produces **spores,** which give rise to the next generation of gametophytes.

questions.question: The country can improve its balance of payments by devaluation when the sum of elasticity of demand for exports and imports is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**greater than unity.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Devaluation** is the **reduction** in the value of a **country's currency relative** to other currencies.
 
• The** elasticity of demand** refers to the responsiveness of** demand for a good or service** to a change in its price.
 
• When the** sum of elasticity **of demand for** exports and imports **is **greater than unity,** a** devaluation** can improve the balance of payments.
 
• This is because a devaluation makes **exports cheaper and imports more expensive**, which can increase the** demand for exports** and **reduce the demand for imports**, thereby** improving the balance of payments**.
 
• When the** sum of elasticity** of demand for **exports and imports **is less than **unity or equal to unity**, devaluation may not be effective in** improving the balance of payments.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• If the sum of elasticity of demand for exports and imports is **less than unity**, devaluation may not lead to a significant increase in demand for exports or decrease in demand for imports.
 
• If the sum of elasticity of demand for exports and imports is** equal to unity,** devaluation may lead to a proportionate increase in demand for exports and decrease in demand for imports, but may not necessarily improve the balance of payments. 
 
• If the sum of elasticity of demand for exports and imports is** zero**, devaluation will not have any effect on the demand for exports or imports, and hence will not improve the balance of payments.

questions.question: India borrowed the DPSP from the ______ Constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Irish.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **DPSP** stands for **Directive Principles of State Policy, **which are guidelines for the government to ensure** social and economic justice **in India.
 
• The Indian Constitution borrowed the concept of DPSP from the** Irish Constitution,** which had similar provisions.
 
• The Irish Constitution's DPSP was influenced by the **Catholic social teachings** and the **ideas of social justice.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Australian Constitution** has no DPSP, but it has provisions related to the** division of powers** between the federal and state governments.

 
 
• The Australian Constitution is the** country's highest law.**
 
• The six autonomous British colonies in Australia—**New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Tasmania, Victoria, and Western Australia**—conducted a series of conventions between **1891 and 1898** to draft the Constitution. 
 
 
 
• The** German Constitution** has a similar concept called** Grundgesetz, **which includes** fundamental rights and principles** for the state's welfare.
 
• Approved in Bonn on **May 8, 1949, **the West German Constitution went into force on** May 23**, following its approval on** May 12** by the occupying **western Allies of World War II.**

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about granite?

options.text: Granite is the most abundant rock in the continental crust.
It is the most common sedimentary rock.
These are igneous rocks that form when hot, molten rock crystallises and solidifies.
Granite is composed mainly of quartz and feldspar with minor amounts of mica.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is the most common sedimentary rock.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Granite** is indeed the **most abundant rock **in the** continental crust.**
 
• Granite is not a sedimentary rock, but an **igneous rock.**
 
• Granite forms from **hot, molten rock** that solidifies over time.
 
• Granite is composed mainly of** quartz and feldspar** with minor amounts of **mica.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Granite is an** intrusive igneous rock,** which means it forms from magma that cools and solidifies beneath the Earth's surface.
 
• It is commonly used as a** building material**, particularly for countertops and flooring.
 
• The minerals that make up granite can vary depending on the** location and conditions of its formation**.
 
• Other minerals that may be present in granite include **amphibole, biotite, and pyroxene.**

questions.question: 'Back to Vedas' was the slogan of which Reform Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arya Samaj.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **slogan "Back to Vedas" **was raised by the **Arya Samaj,** a Hindu reform movement founded by **Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875. **
 
• The Arya Samaj aimed to **purify Hinduism** by returning to the original teachings of the **Vedas **and rejecting later additions and corruptions.
 
• The movement emphasized the importance of **education,** particularly for women, and promoted social reforms such as the** abolition of child marriage and the caste system.**
 
• The Arya Samaj also played a role in** India's independence movement** and supported the **Swadeshi movement** to boycott British goods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dev Samaj** was a reform movement founded by** Pandit Shiv Narayan Agnihotri **in the late 19th century**. **
 
• **Brahmo Samaj **was a reform movement founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy **in the early 19th century that aimed to promote **monotheism and social reforms **such as the abolition of sati and the promotion of women's education.
 
• **Prarthana Samaj **was a reform movement founded by **Atmaram Pandurang** in the late 19th century that sought to promote** monotheism and social reforms **such as the abolition of caste and the promotion of women's education.

questions.question:
Which among the following statements about judicial review in India are correct?

A. Judicial review means that the courts of law have the power of testing the validity of legislative as well as other governmental action with reference to the provisions of the Constitution.

B. Under Article 23 of the Indian Constitution, the compulsion of judicial review was described in the Fundamental Rights in Part III.

C. The power of judicial review is significantly vested upon the High Courts and the Supreme Court of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A and C only.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Statement A is** correct **because it defines the **concept of judicial review **and its scope in India.
 
• Statement B is** incorrect **because there is** no provision** in the Indian Constitution that describes the compulsion of judicial review in the Fundamental Rights in Part III.
 
• Statement C is **correct** because the power of judicial review is significantly vested upon the **High Courts and the Supreme Court **of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial review **is an important feature of the Indian Constitution that ensures the** supremacy of the Constitution **and the** rule of law**.
 
• The power of judicial review enables the judiciary to check the** abuse of power by the legislature** and the executive and to** protect the rights and liberties of the citizens.**
 
• The Indian Constitution's **Article 13 **outlines the procedures for judicial review.
 
• It requires the Indian State to** uphold and execute** the fundamental right.
 
• Additionally, it gives the courts the authority to declare a law or action** unconstitutional** if it violates a** fundamental right.**

• The** India State of Forest Report** is a **biennial publication** by the **Forest Survey of India (FSI)** that provides information on the forest cover of India.

questions.question: 'Ras-Lila' recognised as one of the classical dance forms of India belongs to which of the following states?

• **Ras-Lila** is a **traditional dance** form of **Manipur.**
 
• Ras-Lila is a form of classical dance that depicts the love story of **Lord Krishna and Radha.**
 
• The dance form is performed by both **male and female dancers** wearing traditional Manipuri attire.
 
• The dance is accompanied by traditional Manipuri music and instruments like **pung, pena, and harmonium.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipur** is also known for other traditional dance forms like **Nata Sankirtana, Thang-Ta, and Pung Cholom.**
 
• **Assam's Bihu dance **is a celebration of the** harvest season** and is performed by both men and women.
 
• **Meghalaya's Nongkrem dance** is a part of the annual Nongkrem festival and is performed by the** Khasi tribe.**
 
• **Tripura's Hozagiri dance **is performed by the** Reang tribe** and is a part of their harvest festival.

questions.question: The Amara-Nayakas were ______ in Vijayanagara Empire.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**military commanders.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Amara-Nayakas **were **military commanders** in the** Vijayanagara Empire.**
 
• They were appointed to** govern and protect** various regions of the empire.
 
• The term "Amara-Nayaka" literally means **"commander of an army".**
 
• They were responsible for **maintaining law and order** in their respective regions and also for collecting taxes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Forced labourers **were usually **prisoners of war or people** who were forced to work on public projects.
 
• **Finance officers **were responsible for managing the **finances of the empire**.
 
• **Ordinary peasants** were farmers who worked on the land and paid taxes to the **Amara-Nayakas.**

questions.question: The 'Jal Kranti Abhiyan' was launched by which government during the financial year 2015-2016?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The** Jal Kranti Abhiyan **is a campaign launched by the **Government of India** to create **awareness** about the importance of **water conservation** and management in the country.
 
• The campaign aimed to promote the** conservation of water resources** and to ensure the **optimal utilization of wate**r through various measures like** rainwater harvesting, watershed development, and water resource management**.
 
• The campaign was launched with the objective of making water conservation a **people's movement **and to encourage the participation of all stakeholders in the process.
 
• The campaign also focused on the **revival of traditional water conservation** methods and the adoption of modern technologies to manage and conserve water resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Government of Punjab **has launched several initiatives for water conservation and management, such as the** 'Paani Bachao, Punjab Bachao' campaign **and** the 'Pani Ki Chetna' program.**
 
• The** Government of Haryana** has also launched various programs for water conservation, such as the '**Jal Hi Jeevan Hai' campaign and the 'Mera Pani, Meri Virasat' program.**
 
• The** Government of Uttar Pradesh** has launched several initiatives for water conservation and management, such as the '**Jal Sanrakshan Abhiyan' **and** the 'Har Ghar Jal' program. **
